name: Data Integrity for Manufacturing AI
title: Data Integrity for Manufacturing AI
answer: Data used to train and run manufacturing AI must meet the same integrity standards as other GMP data: attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate. The FDA's data integrity guidance applies to the records AI systems create and use.

reading.body:
Manufacturing AI inherits GMP data integrity rules: training data become controlled records when a model supports quality decisions. ALCOA, meaning attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate, applies to the records AI systems create and use, and the FDA's data integrity guidance covers them.

The practical consequence is that the data pipeline is now a records system. A model's training set has to be traceable to its origin, its labelling and later changes have to be recorded, and outputs used in decisions have to be stored alongside the model version and the context that produced them. Any transformation inside an AI pipeline must preserve the link back to the original record.

This matters for AI specifically because the usual failure mode is not a wrong prediction but an untraceable one. A model that supports a GMP decision cannot be defended if the data behind it cannot be reconstructed, and regulators have repeatedly cited data integrity failures in inspections. The governance burden lands on data lineage and versioning rather than on model accuracy.

The data covers the principle and one dated regulatory action, the FDA's December 2018 final guidance on data integrity and drug CGMP. It does not quantify inspection findings, name specific AI systems, or describe how any manufacturer has implemented this. The ALCOA extension to complete, consistent, enduring and available is mentioned but not applied to AI pipelines here.

explainer:
Data integrity means records are complete, consistent and accurate throughout their life. The common shorthand is ALCOA: attributable to who created them, legible, contemporaneous with the activity, original or a true copy, and accurate, often extended to ALCOA plus with complete, consistent, enduring and available. Regulators have repeatedly cited data integrity failures in inspections.

AI brings data integrity into new places. Training data become records when a model supports GMP decisions, so their origin, labelling and changes must be traceable. Model outputs used in decisions must be stored with the model version and context. And any data transformation in an AI pipeline must preserve the link back to original records.

Why data integrity is the first question

Inspectors have a settled framework for data: it must be attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate, with the additions of complete, consistent, enduring and available. AI puts pressure on every one of those. A model's output is attributable to a software version, not a person. Training data may have been cleaned or sampled in ways that break the link to the original record. And a model updated silently by a vendor is no longer the version that was validated.

The specific risks

Three stand out. Training data provenance: if the plant cannot show where the data came from and that it was not edited, the model built on it is suspect. Version control: inputs, model version, parameters and outputs need to be recorded together for every decision, or an investigation later cannot reconstruct what happened. Human overrides: when an operator disagrees with the model, both the model's output and the override need to be captured, because the pattern of overrides is itself evidence about whether the model works.

How plants handle it

The practical answer is to treat the model like an instrument. It has an identity, a qualification record, a calibration equivalent in the form of performance monitoring, and a change history. Its data flows through the same validated systems as everything else rather than through a data scientist's laptop. That is less exciting than the model itself, but it is what lets the plant answer an inspector's question in minutes rather than weeks.
